Ten comments

This tune is from an old collection which I am unable to identify (no title pages etc).

↳ Posted by fidicen on December 31st, 2002.

The Navvy On The Shore

Misnamed on the Bothy Band’s 1st album as The Navvy On The Line. The real Navvy On The Line is a completely different tune - a James Hill hornpipe also on the database @ https://thesession.org/tunes/4376

↳ Posted by Dr. Dow on May 14th, 2006.

There’s a nicer setting of this tune here: https://thesession.org/tunes/6193

↳ Posted by Dr. Dow on December 29th, 2006.

The Navvy On The Shore, X:2

Some combination of the previous setting, settings here https://thesession.org/tunes/4857 transposed to Dmaj, and Rawlins Cross recording:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Qhxxlj0VKP0

↳ Posted by NfldWhistler on October 16th, 2018.

The Navvy On The Shore, X:4

Catherine McEvoy’s version from “Comb Your Hair and Curl It.” I love how she hits the high G rolls in the B part just a bit early -- very flutey.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VoSIC-dJZic

↳ Posted by B-bird on January 17th, 2024.

The Navvy On The Shore, X:5

Sounds like the Northumbrian version of Neil Gow. Here’s a quote from Wikipedia:

James Hill (c.1811 – 1853) was a British fiddler-composer and publican. Born in Dundee, his family moved to Newcastle upon Tyne and he lived there or Gateshead for the remainder of his short life. He is famous as the composer of many fine common-time hornpipes for fiddle, including The High Level Bridge, The Beeswing, The Hawk and The Omnibus.

↳ Posted by Jim Sime on January 18th, 2025.

The Navvy On The Shore, X:6

A Sligo fiddle version from Maeve Donnelly on the 1983 album Sailing Into Walpole’s Marsh. She picked it up from the playing of Fred Finn.

↳ Posted by Dr. Dow on May 11th, 2026.

The Navvy On The Shore, X:7

The Sligo version from a YouTube video of Fisherstreet playing live https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BYvz-gUJad8. I think they must have got it from Maeve Donnelly or her original source Fred Finn because it’s clearly a variant of the same setting and they have some of the same variations.

↳ Posted by Dr. Dow on May 11th, 2026.

The original link is thesession.org/tunes/1273
